diagnostics.subject: --llm-transport choices / --io
diagnostics.detail: cli.mdx documents `--llm-transport <cli|agent|api>` and `--io <dir>`, matching today's code exactly. The reference deliberately narrows the choices to `cli|api` and drops `--io` per the Phase-0 decision above.

diagnostics.subject: --diff
diagnostics.detail: cli.mdx describes `--diff` as "Run diff check against the committed baseline". Code analyzes the WORKING TREE (diff mode never stashes) and compares it against `.truecourse/LATEST.json`, whose commit may be any earlier analysis — commander's own help says "Run diff check against latest analysis".

diagnostics.subject: non-interactive requiredness
diagnostics.detail: cli.mdx does not record that `--llm`/`--no-llm` is REQUIRED in a non-interactive shell (exit 1 with guidance otherwise), nor that `--stash`/`--no-stash` becomes required non-interactively when the tree is dirty.

diagnostics.subject: --stash in --diff mode
diagnostics.detail: cli.mdx lists `--stash` / `--no-stash` as analyze flags without noting that diff mode accepts them for symmetry and ignores them (diff always analyzes the working tree).

diagnostics.subject: flag conflict precedence
diagnostics.detail: cli.mdx does not state what happens when both halves of a pair are passed. Code: `--llm`/`--no-llm` and `--stash`/`--no-stash` are last-one-wins (single commander property); `--install-skills` beats `--no-skills` regardless of order (separate properties, `installSkills` checked first).

diagnostics.subject: analyze flag set
diagnostics.detail: Every flag in cli.mdx exists in code and every flag in code is documented (`--diff`, `--llm`, `--no-llm`, `--llm-transport`, `--io`, `--stash`, `--no-stash`, `--install-skills`, `--no-skills`). diagnostics.detail: cli.mdx describes `hooks run` only as "Run the pre-commit checks (called by the hook itself)". Code shows it OVERWRITES `.truecourse/diff.json`, takes the repo's `.analyze.lock`, may register the repo, and exits 1 when no baseline exists — none of which is documented on the CLI reference page.

diagnostics.subject: exit codes
diagnostics.detail: cli.mdx documents no exit codes for the hooks commands. Code: `install` exits 0 on a declined confirmation, 1 on a foreign hook; `uninstall` exits 0 when nothing is installed, 1 on a foreign hook; `status` exits 1 on a malformed hooks.yaml; `run` exits 0 for every skip path and 130 on SIGINT.

diagnostics.subject: policy-file location and creation

No implicit `help [command]` subcommand at the root. Commander only adds it to a command that has subcommands AND no action handler; the program registers `program.action(() => program.outputHelp())`, so `truecourse help rules` prints the ROOT help rather than the `rules` help (probe-verified). Group commands that have no action handler (`rules`, `hooks`, `spec`, `guard`, `config`, `telemetry`) DO carry `help [command]`.

`-V, --version` and `-h, --help` resolve on every subcommand, not just the program: `truecourse analyze --version`, `truecourse rules -V` and `truecourse hooks status --version` all print `0.8.0` and exit 0 (probe-verified). The program-level `preAction` hook is the one piece of behavior every subcommand inherits: before ANY subcommand action, `runLlmFirstRun` may open the LLM-transport wizard on stdin. It is skipped for the bare root, for `config llm *` and `hooks run`, when the command passed `--llm-transport`, when `TRUECOURSE_LLM_TRANSPORT` is set, when a transport is already saved in `~/.truecourse/config.json`, and when stdin is not a TTY. Each subcommand journey repeats it as its first stdin interaction.
